newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Transavia starts flights to Sri Lanka.
newsitem.headline: Transavia starts flights to Sri Lanka.

text.p: Dutch Transavia Airlines said on Tuesday it had received permission to start a twice-per-week service to Sri Lanka and the Maldives.

The airline, which mainly operates flights for tourists and which is 80 percent owned by flag carrier KLM Royal Dutch Airlines, said it would start the year-round service in April and added it would use a Boeing 757 with 218 seats.

Transavia said it was in talks with tour operators who are interested in flying holiday makers to Sri Lanka. The service to the Sri Lankan capital of Colombo became available after KLM announced it would stop this route.
